hero.title: Rapido x Navier - India's mobility challenger, on the water
hero.subtitle: India is 7,500 km of coastline, harbours, backwaters and island archipelagos. No platform owns the water yet.
hero.what_we_do_together: We launch a Rapido-branded foiling water tier across India's densest coastal flows - Mumbai's harbour and Alibaug coast, Goa's beaches and rivers, Kochi's backwaters, and the Andaman islands - booked in-app, value-led, category-defining. Navier brings the software-defined hydrofoiling fleet and the network playbook proven in the Maldives; Rapido brings the demand, the app and home-turf reach across India.

why_now: Foiling lifts the hull clear of the water: faster, ~10x more efficient per passenger-mile, smooth and near-silent, hybrid-capable with no charging dependency, and autonomy-ready. A ~100-vessel network is already ramping in the Maldives next door; Kochi's electric Water Metro proves India's clean-ferry appetite; and India's busiest coastal flows - Mumbai<->Alibaug, Port Blair<->Havelock - run on slow, ageing diesel craft. The category gets claimed cluster-by-cluster.
multimodal_fit: Rapido already runs the hard parts - real-time demand, dispatch, dynamic pricing and a vast captain-partner network across India. A foiling water tier slots straight in: same app, captain-partners on the water, the water leg booked door-to-door with the Rapido auto or bike to and from the jetty.

differentiation.why_navier: Software-defined and autonomy-ready; a factory in Turkey for supply; and a ~100-vessel network already proving the model in the Maldives - directly relevant to India's coastline and archipelagos. The water is the ownable surface Rapido's rivals ignore.

why_navier_now.step_change: Hydrofoiling lifts the hull clear of the water, so a Navier vessel flies instead of plowing through chop - roughly 10x more efficient than a conventional planing boat, faster (30+ kt cruise), and dramatically smoother and quieter. network_thesis.headline: One app. India's 7,500 km coastline. The water layer of India's mobility challenger.
network_thesis.body: India is a coastline of harbours, tidal rivers, backwaters and island archipelagos - and no mobility platform owns the water. The same in-app foiling tier proven in the Maldives extends to every coastal flow Rapido serves on land: Mumbai's harbour, Goa's coast, Kerala's backwaters and the Andaman islands. Pick one market to prove it, or roll the recommended sequence. The fleet, app integration and captain-partner model are identical everywhere.
network_thesis.how_to_read: Each card is a real, ready market. Start with Mumbai - Rapido's biggest battleground and the harbour with the most proven water demand - or pick any cluster. The phased sequence below is our recommended path.
network_thesis.coverage_note: Rapido is India's fastest-rising mobility platform, multi-format across the country's metros and tourism states; these four markets are where the coastal water demand is densest today. The same fleet and in-app tier extend to every harbour, river and island corridor Rapido serves on land.

partner_context.their_pressure: Andaman inter-island transport is captive to diesel fast-ferries with no premium or clean tier.
partner_context.where_navier_fits: A foiling tier gives Rapido an ownable island-hopping product on India's busiest tropical archipelago - Port Blair<->Havelock<->Neil - in-app.

markets.why_now: Andaman island tourism is booming on sold-out diesel ferries, the government is pushing connectivity, and Rapido is expanding into high-growth tourism geographies.

why_navier_now.step_change: Hydrofoiling lifts the hull clear of the water, so a Navier vessel flies instead of plowing through chop - roughly 10x more efficient than a conventional planing boat, faster (30+ kt cruise), and dramatically smoother and quieter. It's software-defined and autonomy-ready, so the same fleet keeps getting better and cheaper to run over time. A step-change in marine mobility, not an incremental faster boat.
why_navier_now.no_new_infrastructure: Navier rides on infrastructure that already exists - the open ocean and the berths and jetties already in use. No vertiports, no new rights-of-way, no tunnels or tracks. Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal; the Quanta-LR hybrid needs no charging infrastructure at all. That's the fundamental contrast with flying taxis and other new-infrastructure modes: nothing to permit, build, or wait for.
why_navier_now.the_moment: India's busiest island-hop - Port Blair<->Havelock - sells out every season on diesel fast-ferries, in coral-sensitive waters that reward clean propulsion, with no premium tier for Rapido to ride.

proof_points.claim: Port Blair<->Havelock is India's busiest island-hop.
proof_points.evidence: ~38 nm on diesel fast-ferries that sell out in peak season - a captive, high-margin tourism corridor.

proof_points.claim: The star islands drive the demand.
proof_points.evidence: Havelock (Radhanagar Beach) and Neil are top domestic-honeymoon and diving destinations.

proof_points.claim: Coral-sensitive marine parks reward clean propulsion.
proof_points.evidence: The Mahatma Gandhi Marine National Park and surrounding reefs make zero-wake foiling an environmental asset over diesel ferries.
Central focus on island tourism and connectivity under Maritime India Vision 2030 provides a policy tailwind.

objections.concern: The islands are remote with limited infrastructure.
objections.response: Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal at existing jetties; the Quanta-LR hybrid needs no charging infrastructure at all - ideal for remote-island operations.
Peak tourism is the calm Oct-May window; foils handle shoulder-season chop better than the diesel fast-ferries.
Marine-tourism operators already work within the A&N Administration's framework - we build on the established path.

the_ask.partner_brings: Demand, the rider/guest relationship, and Andaman & Nicobar Islands as the launch market to prove the on-water tier.
